references.text: Isaiah 9:6 describes the coming Messiah as an eternal ruler, which reflects the people's expectation that 'the Christ remains forever' in John 12:34.

Isaiah 53:12 predicts that the Messiah will be 'lifted up' (highly exalted) and counted among the wicked, which directly corresponds to the question of why the 'Son of Man' must be 'lifted up' in John 12:34.
Ezekiel 34:23-24 speaks of a single shepherd, David's servant, who will rule forever, supporting the people's understanding of an eternal Messiah in John 12:34.
In John 3:14, Jesus compares himself to Moses lifting up the serpent in the wilderness and explains that the Son of Man must be 'lifted up', which is central to the discussion in John 12:34.

In John 8:28, Jesus says that when the 'Son of Man' is lifted up, people will know that he is, which provides the direct context for the people's question about the identity of the one who is lifted up in John 12:34.
